messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Covariance Matrix Sensitivity
parts:
Where is the covariance matrix type defined? I'm having a hell of a time where it shows up in the model tests as it seems to spit out zero-valued diagonals even for seemingly reasonable (O(1)) values of the unconstrained parameters, momenta, and gradients. For example, models/bugs_examples/vol3/camel/camel2 dies after a single iteration with either the transformed parameter rho becomes a nan (because Sigma[1,1] or Sigma[2,2] is vanishing) or Sigma itself throws a "not positive-definite" exception.

Additionally, if anyone can tell me how to access constrained parameters via the model object I'd be very much appreciative.

Thanks!

-Mike

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Covariance Matrix Sensitivity
parts:
Did you change the MCMC algorithms? I don't understand why
your samplers would be behaving differently than the ones
currently in master.

The transform is described near the end of the manual in
the transforms chapter.

For the code, you can look at stan/prob/transform to see
where the transform is happening (through io/reader and io/writer).

In the generated code for a model, look at
transform_inits() for where a writer is used
for the transforms for variables read from
a context (base class implemented by file for the
command line and through R for RStan).

You then see the constraining transform getting called
through a reader in the log_prob functions.

The write_array() method takes unconstrained params and
inverse transforms to constrained parameters and then
writes the real ones to an array. This follows the
same format as write_csv(), writing the parameters out
in row-major order in the order they were declared.
The output is constrained. write_csv_header() writes
out the "names" of the parameters, including the
indices of an array --- this is the header dumped out
in the output from the command.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Covariance Matrix Sensitivity
parts:
> Did you change the MCMC algorithms? I don't understand why
> your samplers would be behaving differently than the ones
> currently in master.

The only real change is going from different "effective" step sizes for each parameter to a single step size and a proper mass matrix. This required significant changes in the adaptation, but the new code works for most models.

The problem with the covariance matrix models isn't with the MCMC - the evolution diverges but the resulting proposal would just be rejected. The diverging state, however, causes the covariance transform to throw an exception before the transition can be rejected. I'm not sure why the previous samplers aren't vulnerable to the same problem.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Covariance Matrix Sensitivity
parts:
The previous samplers caught exceptions and treated
them as an instant rejection. They also did the same
thing with -infinity and NaN returns.

We have our functions configured with exceptions
so that then we can record an error message to report
when it's caught.

So far, the messages aren't very good, because they're
not located with respect to the user model -- they just
say which function was called and what the problem was
with the parameters it was called with.

To get better messages, we'd need to pass more information
to the functions from the model, such as the line number
of the call in the Stan model (not the C++ code).
Or we could dream up some alternative. (For instance, we could
put a try/catch around every function call :-))

- Bob
